subject: Surge buffer / overage structure — clarification and proposal
messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@ingenuity.ai>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@ingenuity.ai
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on minimums and on-demand top-up rates

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the walk-through earlier. Procurement asked me to get the details in writing around two things before we proceed:

1) Minimum monthly financial commitment (we call it a ‘floor’) — you mentioned a soft floor where Ingenuity could dip below but with a true-up. Need explicit numbers and consequences.
2) On-demand / surge pricing — If we exceed committed throughput, what is the per-token on-demand rate versus the discounted commit rate? Any caps, daily burst windows, or automatic throttles?

We expect a baseline of ~250M tokens/month for Q4, with spikes up to ~1.2B tokens/day for short experiments. For budgeting I need an example month that shows cost under: baseline, 3x spike day, and sustained 2x week.

Can you also confirm whether unused committed spend rolls over, or if you offer buffer credits we can tap during a surge?

Appreciate a written proposal we can share with finance and procurement.

Best,
Sarah Kim\Director, Product\Ingenuity AI
Attachment: ingenuity_expected_volumes.csv (csv)

From: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@ingenuity.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on minimums and on-demand top-up rates

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the clear ask. I pulled together a concise proposal and included two optional structures we typically use for customers with bursty workloads. See the short summary below; full breakdown attached (redwood_pricing_v2.pdf).

Summary (examples use your 250M tokens/mo baseline):
- Commit tier: 250M tokens/month at $0.0007/token (12-month agreement).
- Soft minimum (monthly floor): 80% of committed spend/month (financial true-up applies if below). In practice: if monthly usage is <200M tokens, Ingenuity pays the difference between actual spend and floor at the commit rate.
- On-demand (overage) rate: $0.0012/token (approximately 71% premium to commit rate).
- Surge buffer credit pool (optional add-on): pre-purchase a pool of buffer credits (e.g., 200M tokens) at the commit rate; credits auto-draw during spikes and do not expire during the contract year.

Options:
A) No buffer: standard commit + on-demand overage billing. True-up monthly against 80% floor.
B) Buffer credits: pay +$X/month to maintain a buffer pool we draw from before charging on-demand rates; any unused credits roll to the next quarter.

Attachments: detailed monthly cost scenarios and a one-page example month with 3x spike day.

Next steps: if you prefer, we can model a 12-month spend schedule and show the net cost delta between A and B. Laura and Marcus are cc'd to help with the buffer sizing and contract language.

Cheers,
Alex Martinez\Enterprise Sales\Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_pricing_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Procurement <procurement@ingenuity.ai>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on minimums and on-demand top-up rates

Alex / Laura —

Two quick clarifying questions before we escalate to legal:

1) True-up timing: is the true-up settled monthly or quarterly? We prefer quarterly to smooth billing, but understand operationally you may need monthly.
2) Overage cap / graduated pricing: can you provide a tiered on-demand schedule (e.g., 0-1B tokens/day at $0.0012, 1B-3B/day at $0.00095) rather than a single flat surcharge? Having a step-down as volume increases significantly helps our finance forecasting.

Also: in the buffer option — can unused buffer credits roll forward across quarters (you indicated yes) and would there be a maximum rollover (e.g., 2x purchased buffer)?

We attached a simplified monthly profile for Q4 to sanity-check the numbers.

Thanks,
Procurement Team\Ingenuity AI
Attachment: ingenuity_q4_profile.pdf (pdf)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Procurement <procurement@ingenuity.ai>, alex_martinez@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on minimums and on-demand top-up rates

Hi Sarah / Procurement —

Thanks for the practical asks. Proposed refinements below (keeps you protected, keeps Redwood covered):

- True-up cadence: quarterly by default (3-month smoothing). If monthly reporting is desired we can provide it but settlement is quarterly.
- Graduated on-demand tiers (daily peak basis):
  * 0–1B tokens/day: $0.00120/token
  * 1B–3B tokens/day: $0.00098/token
  * >3B tokens/day: $0.00085/token (requires pre-clearance for sustained >3B/day to avoid accidental budget spikes)
- Buffer credits:
  * Can be purchased at commit rate and are available to draw in any month.
  * Unused credits roll forward quarter-to-quarter for up to 2 quarters (max 2x purchased buffer cap).
- Minimum floor: 80% of committed monthly tokens, but billed on a quarterly true-up at the commit rate (so effectively 80% * 3 months).

Examples included in the attached spreadsheet. If this looks acceptable we'll add language into the SOW: quarterly true-up, graduated on-demand tiers, buffer purchase option with 2-quarter rollover.

Action: please confirm preferred path (A: standard commit + graduated on-demand; B: commit + buffer pool (we will model cost)).

Regards,
Laura Bennett\Senior Manager, Commercial Strategy\Redwood Inference
